scope: Historical family inventory and study evidence through Phase61; Phase62 submitted snapshot only. No training jobs, test-role access, or fresh physics evaluation performed. Not every raw artifact byte was re-audited.

tracked_evidence.scientific_question: Which phase-3/4 pretraining checkpoint gives the best downstream level-reconstruction validation performance under an otherwise identical frozen-transfer run?
Does the step-54064 exploratory baseline retain its small rollout edge-F1 advantage over the best pretraining-complete step-81096 checkpoint on two new disjoint validation cohorts?

Can globally depth-balanced replay, rollout-conditioned training with protected teacher supervision, and conservative late encoder adaptation improve the observed one-level reconstruction collapse while preserving structural validity?

arm_roles.hypothesis: A globally depth-balanced, four-train-size-equivalent replay budget improves depth even when unrepresentable predicted contexts retain historical teacher fallback.

Masking targets that cannot be represented in predicted context while retaining a 0.25 auxiliary teacher loss avoids false no-object supervision and protects link learning without arbitrary recovery logits.
Unfreezing the exactly transferred encoder halfway through training at 0.05 times decoder LR improves rollout-conditioned representations beyond the frozen masked-context arm.

tracked_evidence.scientific_question: Does all-level loss weighting plus explicit recovery supervision, with a preregistered 0.35 pointer threshold, improve semantic full-decay hierarchy recovery over the controlled phase35-style baseline?

arm_roles.hypothesis: The corrected selection rule alone is the controlled reference.
Increasing loss weight toward levels 3-6 and explicit recovery supervision improves root, LCAG, and exact-mother recovery.

tracked_evidence.scientific_question: Does increasing auxiliary teacher anchoring from 0.25 to 0.50, while holding the successful phase36 weighted/recovery contract fixed, improve exact hierarchy recovery without losing rollout recall?

arm_roles.hypothesis: Repeating the successful phase36 weighted/recovery contract on a fresh cohort provides the paired reference.
Stronger auxiliary teacher anchoring improves exact mother/link assignment and half-tree precision while retaining the phase36 depth and source-recall gains.

tracked_evidence.scientific_question: Does increasing the pointer-positive loss weight from 16 to 24, while holding the phase37 teacher-anchored weighted/recovery contract fixed, recover exact mothers and roots without exhausting precision?

arm_roles.hypothesis: Repeating the phase37 teacher-anchor candidate with the established pointer-positive weight provides the paired reference.
A stronger positive pointer loss recovers missing daughter links and enables nonzero exact-mother, LCAG, and root completion while the preregistered precision gates limit false associations.

tracked_evidence.scientific_question: Does increasing the pointer-positive loss weight from 24 to 32, while holding the best phase38 teacher-anchored weighted/recovery contract fixed, produce reproducible hierarchy recovery without exhausting precision?

arm_roles.hypothesis: Repeating the best phase38 pointer-24 candidate on a fresh cohort provides the paired reference after its one-root result failed a clean cross-environment replay.
Additional positive pointer weight increases complete daughter-link recall and root recovery while stricter precision and hierarchy gates limit false associations.

tracked_evidence.scientific_question: Does doubling reconstruction data and training exposure improve hierarchy recovery, and does added per-level query capacity provide a further controlled gain without exhausting precision?

arm_roles.hypothesis: The phase39 pointer-32 architecture receives exactly twice the training data and twice its four-size-equivalent step budget.
More decoder query slots reduce competition among simultaneous mothers while leaving encoder size, data, optimizer, and losses fixed.

tracked_evidence.scientific_question: Does doubling reconstruction data and training exposure improve hierarchy recovery, and does added per-level query capacity provide a further controlled gain without exhausting precision?

arm_roles.hypothesis: The phase39 pointer-32 architecture receives exactly twice the training data and twice its four-size-equivalent step budget.

tracked_evidence.scientific_question: Does a level-specific pointer class-balance correction improve exact full-decay topology without sacrificing the phase40r1 control's depth, source recall, or tree validity?

arm_roles.hypothesis: The phase40r1 winning decoder is reproduced on the untouched phase41 cohort with its scalar pointer-positive weight of 32.
Reducing only the level-1 pointer-positive weight from 32 to 24 will reduce low-level over-linking while preserving the higher-level pointer recall needed for complete roots.
